subject: VALUE clause
notes: kb/Work PB921 LANDED. The row read CONFORMS while SR6 reached only two of the four VALUE formats it governs. SR6 has TWO halves -- the literal-FORM rule (fixed-point vs floating-point) and the EDITION on which a numeric literal became writable at all, dated by Annex E.3.3 item 43 as a COBOL-2023 addition -- and they were written in two places: the form half in DataBinder.ValidateValueCategory, which the item VALUE, the level-88 set and the group VALUE all funnel through, and the edition half INLINE in DataBinder.ScreenValueLiteral, which only the item VALUE reaches. The two places covered different formats. MEASURED on this worktree's own build, before: at --std 85 `01 X PIC ZZ9.99 VALUE 10.` (format 1) drew COBOL0900, `05 E PIC ZZ9.99 OCCURS 2 VALUE 10 FROM (1) TO (2).` (format 2) drew it, `01 X PIC ZZ9.99. 88 X-TEN VALUE 10.` (format 3) compiled clean and stored the COBOL-2023 edited image ` 10.00`, and `03 COLUMN 1 PIC ZZ9.99 VALUE 10.` (format 4 -- a format SR6 NAMES) compiled clean and PRINTED it, because a report entry's VALUE operands pass through neither screen. Both halves now live in one method, asked from ValidateValueCategory (formats 1, 2, 3, group) and from the report bind once the printable picture is settled (format 4); measured after, all four are refused at 85/2002/2014 and accepted at 2023. OVERTURNED BY kb/Work PB3566 (wave 1157 D): the literal zero is a numeric literal, so SR6's edition gates `VALUE 0` and `VALUE 0.0` too (COBOL0900 at 85/2002/2014; the one pre-2023 zero was the FIGURATIVE ZERO, Annex E.2 item 28, still unrefused at every edition), because SR6's last sentence ('the integer and decimal forms of the literal zero may also be specified for either format') separates the fixed-point from the floating-point formats INSIDE the 2023 permission and is no all-edition exemption; the fuzz run fuzz-20261022-163846 found it (12 programs, GnuCOBOL refuses `VALUE 0` on a numeric-edited item). Only the figurative ZERO/ZEROES and SR7's alphanumeric/national edited image stay unrefused at 85 -- the screen's complement, asserted. DETERMINATION: SR6's text enumerates formats 1, 2 and 4 and omits 3; the omission is read as naming the DATA-ITEM formats rather than as excluding the condition-name one, because 13.18.63.4 GR19 gives a condition-name 'the characteristics of ... its conditional variable', 14.9.39.4 GR6 places the literal 'according to the rules for the VALUE clause' (SR6's conversion), and 13.18.63.3 SR36 carries SR11 -- the numeric-edited EDITING rule -- into format 5, whose subject is a level-88 condition-name exactly as format 3's is. Both readings agree below 2023, which is the half this closes; at 2023 the reading that does not reject source is taken.
